result.builder:
Criteria the build must meet (from the issue, word for word):
- node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
- without --shout the output is unchanged
- docs/index.md documents --shout
- after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Steps:
1. Read bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. Today the CLI takes the first argument that does not start with `--` as the name and prints `Hello, <name>!` followed by a newline. The pages workflow publishes the docs/ directory to GitHub Pages on every push to main.
2. In bin/greet.js, check whether `--shout` is among the arguments. If it is, print the whole greeting line in upper case (for `Ada` that is `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline). The flag must work whether it comes before or after the name. Keep finding the name the same way, so `--shout` is never read as the name. If you put the upper-casing in src/greet.js, add it as a separate export or an optional parameter so that `greeting(name)` still returns exactly `Hello, <name>!`.
3. Without `--shout`, keep the output byte-for-byte the same: `Hello, <name>!` followed by a newline on stdout. Keep the usage message and exit code 2 when no name is given.
4. In test/greet.test.js, add tests for `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` (expect `HELLO, ADA!\n`) and `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`. Keep the existing tests unchanged. Run `npm test` and make sure every test passes.
5. Update docs/index.md to document the `--shout` flag: show a usage line such as `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and say that it prints the greeting in upper case, with an example. Keep the docs in docs/ so the existing pages workflow publishes them. Do not change .github/workflows/pages.yml unless it is needed for docs/index.md to be published.
6. The last criterion can only come true after the PR is merged and the pages workflow deploys. You cannot make it true from the PR. In the PR description, say that `--shout` appears in the published page only after merge and deploy, and that someone needs to check https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ at that point.
7. Open one pull request that contains these changes.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head and run `npm install` if it is needed (the project has no dependencies). Then run `npm test` once and record the result as context. Next, run the checks below in order, one for each expect line, and give each one PASS or FAIL with the commands you ran and their output.

Check 1. Expect line: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
Run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js --shout 'Grace Hopper'`. Also run `node bin/greet.js Ada` and `node bin/greet.js 'Grace Hopper'` to get the normal greetings.
PASS: each `--shout` run exits 0, and its stdout is exactly the upper-cased version of the normal greeting for the same name (for Ada: `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline).
FAIL: a `--shout` run exits non-zero, its output is not upper case, or its output is not the upper-cased normal greeting (for example, `--shout` is treated as the name).

Check 2. Expect line: "without --shout the output is unchanged"
At the PR head, run `node bin/greet.js Ada`, `node bin/greet.js 'Grace Hopper'` and `node bin/greet.js` (with no name), recording stdout, stderr and the exit code for each. Run the same three commands at the PR's base commit (for example, check out the merge-base in a separate worktree) and compare.
PASS: for all three commands, stdout, stderr and the exit code are identical between the base and the PR head. For Ada the output is `Hello, Ada!` followed by a newline.
FAIL: any of the three commands differs between the base and the head.

Check 3. Expect line: "docs/index.md documents --shout"
Run `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` at the PR head, then read the lines it matches.
PASS: docs/index.md contains `--shout` and describes what it does (prints the greeting in upper case, or louder).
FAIL: docs/index.md does not mention `--shout`, or mentions it without saying what it does.

Check 4. Expect line: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"
Run `curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/` and search the response for `--shout`. Record the HTTP status and whether the PR has been merged (`gh pr view --json state,mergedAt`).
PASS: the PR is merged and the fetched published page contains `--shout`.
FAIL: the PR is not merged yet, the page cannot be fetched, or the page does not contain `--shout`. Do not mark this check PASS based on the diff or on docs/index.md. Only the live page counts. If the PR is not merged yet, report FAIL and say that this line can only be checked after merge and deploy.

Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL):
- Check that `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` (flag after the name) also shouts.
- Check that `npm test` passes and that new tests cover `--shout`.
- Check that .github/workflows/pages.yml still publishes the docs directory on pushes to main, so that merging will deploy the updated docs/index.md.
